guides.title: Heart rate

deviceIllustration.altText: Pulse oximeter or manual wrist pulse

steps: If safe, rest for several minutes before measuring.
Use a pulse monitor as described by its manufacturer, or locate the pulse at your wrist.
Read the pulse in beats per minute and record the circumstances.

guides.whyItMatters: Heart-rate changes may reflect activity, stress, sleep, or other influences. A single reading does not establish a diagnosis.

guides.title: Blood pressure

steps: Use the correct cuff size and follow the device instructions.
Sit supported and keep the cuff at approximately heart level if the environment permits.
Start the device, remain still, and record systolic and diastolic readings.

guides.whyItMatters: Blood pressure helps track circulatory changes; position, activity, and technique can affect readings.

guides.title: Oxygen saturation

steps: Rest your hand and remove obstructions if practical.
Place the finger into the oximeter according to the manufacturer.
Wait for a stable displayed value and record the percentage.

guides.whyItMatters: SpO₂ estimates oxygen saturation; oximeter accuracy can be affected by several conditions and device limitations.

guides.title: Body temperature

steps: Choose the approved measurement site for the thermometer.
Wait for the result and record the measured temperature and site in notes.

guides.whyItMatters: Temperature trends help indicate changes in body state, but different measurement sites vary.

guides.title: Sleep log

steps: After waking, estimate actual time asleep rather than just time in bed.
Rate perceived sleep quality from 1 (poor) to 5 (excellent).

guides.whyItMatters: Sleep duration and quality can help monitor fatigue and changes in daily performance.
